meta.campaign: CA3 Zenji sibling hunt / L2 lane

test_definitions.a: keeper/rebalance/liquidation path is callable by an unprivileged EOA (no role, whitelist, veToken or owner approval)
test_definitions.b: the vault values its LP/strategy position and its LTV from a DEX/Curve/Velodrome pool the caller can trade (spot), rather than an oracle/TWAP
test_definitions.c: the vault itself computes the slippage floor (minOut) from that same manipulable pool, or applies no floor at all (caller-supplied minOut does NOT count: the caller then bears the slippage)

candidates.permissionless_evidence: permissionLessLiquidationEnabled() = false (eth_call, block 159337708); liquidatorWhitelist(0x1111..) = false; eth_call from 0x1111.. at block 159337856 reverts Error(string) '20' = VL_LIQUIDATOR_NOT_IN_WHITELIST (Errors.sol in ExtraFinance invariant repo). Same revert for the protocol owner.
candidates.valuation_source: per-vault flag liquidateWithTWAP; 34 of 54 live OP vaults have it false (spot pool reserves), 20 true (TWAP). Implementation unverified; inferred from on-chain flag + IVeloVaultPositionManager interface.
candidates.funds_held_by_contract: VPM holds no tokens; 54 live vaults hold LP staked in Velodrome gauges; 24 of 54 still carry debt shares
candidates.notes: Liquidation is a flag+whitelist keeper path, disabled on both OP and Base. Even if enabled, the caller (liquidator) supplies minOut, so the vault never trades on a pool-derived floor. Adjacent (different) risk if the flag is enabled: 34 OP / 75 Base live vaults are spot-priced (liquidateWithTWAP=false), so a forced-liquidation attack would be conceivable. Direct-to-vault calls also fail: claimRewardsAndReInvestToLiquidity(0x76f7903a) reverts onlyVeloPositionManagerContract on the newer vault code, so the VPM gate cannot be bypassed.
